item.content:encoded:
AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-12

Generated: 2026-11-12 15:44 UTC | Tools covered: 2

  • Claude Code
  • OpenCode
  • Claude Code Skills

Cross-Tool Comparison

AI CLI Tools Cross-Comparison Report, 2026-11-12

Scope: only Claude Code and OpenCode digests were supplied. Other tracked tools (Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Kimi, Qwen, and so on) are not covered, so the conclusions below are limited to these two.

1. Ecosystem Overview

The two communities are at different stages. Claude Code is a closed-source, subscription-metered product, and its discussion centers on quota transparency, account management and model behavior. OpenCode is an open-source, provider-agnostic tool. Its discussion centers on runtime stability (V2 plugins, MCP, SSH), free-tier limits and security. Both are working through the cost of running agents at scale: Claude Code users see opaque metering, and OpenCode users see free-tier caps and declined payments. Both are also seeing cross-session and cross-project context problems.

2. Activity Comparison

Metric Claude Code OpenCode
Hot issues listed 10 10 (plus 2 extra mentions)
Top thread #60705 (296 comments, closed) #59387 free-tier megathread (360 comments)
Highest-voted #18435 multi-account (👍 1032) #4283 clipboard (👍 135)
PRs updated (24h) 0 10+ highlighted
Releases None process-daemon-v0.5.2 (@opencode/pty@0.5.2, a sub-package, not the core CLI)
Triage character Bulk stale-bot closures inflate activity Mix of fixes in flight and closures

Issue counts are as listed in the digests, not total volumes. Claude Code's update numbers overstate fresh activity because of the stale-bot closures. Its PR repo state is also not visible in this data, which suggests development happens mostly outside public PRs.

3. Shared Feature Directions

Need Claude Code OpenCode
Cost and quota transparency #97074 (headless costs about 1.8× more), #91775 (/usage over-counts about 2×), #63930 (cache waste) #59387 (free-tier resets), #60659 (spend estimate in the TUI footer)
Multi-session and context isolation #24798, #86059 (inter-session messaging) #63550 (cross-project context pollution), #48826 (subagent state)
Context and config control #20880 (parent CLAUDE.md exclusion), #81833 (worktree memory) #54375 (model kept across plan/build), #63553 (worktree badges)
Reliable plugin, MCP and connectivity layers #95822 (OAuth refresh), #85979 (ECONNRESET) #52237 (MCP not retried), #49982 (plugin reload)
Non-ASCII text correctness #83033 (Hangul \uXXXX corruption) #63186 (unicode escapes in text)
Git worktree support #81833, #78569 #63553
Desktop and IDE regressions #25128, #93782, #80912 #59461, #52941, #63229

The unicode-escape bug appears in both tools, which points to a shared model or tool-call serialization weakness rather than a single client bug.

4. Differentiation Analysis

  • Product model: Claude Code is a vertically integrated suite spanning CLI, Desktop, Cowork and the VS Code extension. Its requests are about accounts, profiles and Cowork configuration. OpenCode is a horizontal, multi-provider platform. Its requests are about provider catalogs, local-model access (the Unix socket PR #62743 for llama.cpp, Ollama and vLLM) and marketplaces.
  • Target users: Claude Code serves subscription users, including individuals and teams that split work and personal accounts. OpenCode serves free-tier and bring-your-own-model users, self-hosters and remote-SSH developers.
  • Extensibility: OpenCode is pushing a V2 plugin architecture (composer API, TSX plugins, marketplace). It also asks for Claude Code hooks compatibility (#12472), which makes Claude Code's conventions a de facto standard.
  • Security posture: OpenCode users are explicitly asking for sandboxing (#2242, 👍 84). Claude Code's digest shows no comparable thread today.
  • Technical direction: OpenCode is porting its CLI to native (#63477) and handling Windows/PowerShell and SSH. Claude Code's visible work is on the metering and model-behavior side.

5. Community Momentum & Maturity

  • Claude Code: It has a very large and engaged user base (👍 1032 on one request, and several threads above 200 comments). Its public iteration was quiet today, with no release and no PRs. Its pain points are those of a mature, heavily used product: billing, quotas and polish.
  • OpenCode: It iterates rapidly in public, with about 10 notable PRs across core, TUI, SSH and Windows. It is still stabilizing V2, with reload and MCP-retry failures. Its biggest thread (360 comments) is about free-tier limits, which suggests rapid adoption outrunning its operations.
  • Reading: Claude Code has the larger demand signal. OpenCode has the visible development velocity. Neither one is clearly "more mature" across every dimension.

6. Trend Signals

  1. Metering is the new reliability problem. Headless and automation modes are priced and metered differently from interactive use, and developers now audit this. Decision-makers should check per-token cost in CI before they commit to a subscription plan.
  2. Hooks, skills and CLAUDE.md are becoming de facto standards. Compatibility requests suggest that portable agent configuration lowers switching costs.
  3. Multi-session and worktree workflows are mainstream. Parallel agents expose state, memory and context-isolation gaps in both tools.
  4. Sandboxing and trust are rising concerns, driven by the unrequested-action reports on the Claude Code side and the possible cross-context leak and missing sandbox on the OpenCode side.
  5. Internationalization matters for agent tooling. Non-ASCII corruption in tool-call parameters is a correctness issue for CJK users.
  6. Local and self-hosted models are first-class. Unix socket support for local inference servers points to growing demand for hybrid cloud and local setups.

Caveat: This is based on one day of data from two tools. Treat the trends as signals, not conclusions, and confirm them against the wider tracked set (for example Codex, Gemini CLI and Copilot CLI) before making decisions.

Per-Tool Reports

Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code

Claude Code Skills Highlights

Source: anthropics/skills

Claude Code Skills Community Highlights (data as of 2026-11-12)

Data caveat: The Comments field is undefined for every PR in this dataset, so PRs can't be ranked by discussion volume. The PR ranking below uses theme importance, recency of updates, and linked issues instead. Issue comment counts are intact. All 20 PRs shown are OPEN, and none is merged or draft.

1. Top Skills Ranking (PRs)

# PR What it does Highlights Status
1 #1298 skill-creator: isolate trigger evals Fixes false-miss trigger scores: competing per-worker command probes, select() failing on Windows pipes, and runtime failures counted as non-triggers. It targets the same bug as the heavily discussed Issues #1352 (6 comments) and #556 (13 comments). Open (updated 2026-09-16)
2 #1742 mcp-builder: mcp>=2 support Handles the streamablehttp_client → streamable_http_client rename and the new custom-header mechanism. Fixes #1668. This is a breaking-SDK compatibility fix that blocks mcp-builder for new users. Open
3 #1980 webapp-testing: drop shell=True Removes a command-injection risk (CWE-78) in with_server.py. Relates to the trust and security concerns in Issue #492. Open (updated 2026-11-01)
4 #1792 docx: report LibreOffice timeout accept_changes.py now returns an error on timeout. It claims success only after checking that no revision marks remain. Fixes a silent false-success. Open (updated 2026-11-01)
5 #2019 xlsx: resolve scoped defined names external_links_at_risk now catches external links reached through worksheet-scoped names and aliases. Fixes #2013 and removes false negatives. Open (updated 2026-11-03)
6 #1997 skill-creator: correct YAML frontmatter parsing Replaces hand-rolled quote stripping with proper YAML scalar parsing. Fixes metadata drift in the eval and optimization commands. Open
7 #1950 claude-api: pause_turn guidance Updates Python guidance now that SDK 1.1.0 resumes paused turns automatically. Active as of 2026-11-10, the most recent update in this list. Open
8 #525 Pyxel retro-game skill A new skill for creating, debugging, and verifying Pyxel games with headless runs and frame inspection. Open since March, still being updated (2026-11-01). Open

2. Community Demand Trends (Issues)

  1. Reliable skill-creator and eval tooling. Issues #556 (13 comments, 7 👍) and #1352 (6) report near-zero trigger rates. #202 asks for the skill to follow best practice. This is the largest cluster.
  2. Security and trust boundaries. #492 is the most discussed issue, with 46 comments, about community skills impersonating the anthropic/ namespace. The shell-injection PR #1980 belongs here too.
  3. Context and token efficiency. #1487 reports claude-api injecting about 156k tokens in one call. #189 (9 👍) reports duplicate skills from the document-skills and example-skills plugins.
  4. Team and org distribution. #228 (17 comments, 8 👍) asks for org-wide skill sharing instead of passing .skill files around.
  5. Document-skill correctness. #2018 (docx merge_runs.py writes invalid XML) and #1868 (an off-by-one in the slack-gif-creator gradient) are examples.
  6. Agent memory, governance and quality skills. These are proposals, not bugs: #1329 compact-memory, #1385 a reasoning quality-gate pipeline, and #412 agent-governance (closed).
  7. Better skill descriptions and triggering. #2064 says theme-factory describes what it does but not when to use it.

#1143 (16 👍, an account-email change request) is a platform request, not a Skills one.

3. High-Potential Pending Skills

These are the PRs most likely to land. They are small, well-scoped fixes with linked issues and recent activity:

  • #1742: mcp>=2 compatibility. It is a clear bug fix with a linked issue.
  • #1298 and #1997: they fix the skill-creator eval problems behind two high-traffic issues.
  • #1980: a small security hardening change.
  • #1792, #2019, #1734: docx and xlsx robustness fixes.
  • #1950: a docs update tied to an SDK release.
  • Small bug fixes by gerardrecinto: #1977, #1976, #1975.

New-skill PRs such as #525 (Pyxel), #1245, #1703, #1771, and #1615 have sat open for months. Several are niche or vendor-specific, and the open backlog suggests the maintainers are favoring fixes to existing skills over new ones. Treat them as less likely to merge soon.

4. Skills Ecosystem Insight

The community's demand is concentrated on the reliability, security, and context cost of existing official skills, especially skill-creator's eval and trigger accuracy. New-skill proposals get far less traction.

Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-11-12

Today's Highlights

No new releases and no PRs were updated in the last 24 hours. Activity was almost entirely issue triage: many stale or invalid reports were closed in bulk, including the 296-comment /goal model-behavior thread. Open discussion is dominated by usage-metering and billing complaints (headless claude -p consuming the 5-hour window faster than interactive mode), multi-account support, and Korean (Hangul) corruption in tool-call parameters.

Releases

None in the last 24h.

Hot Issues

  1. #60705 — /goal Stop-hook directive cited as authorization for unrequested actions (CLOSED, 296 comments). It is the most-discussed thread. It documents model-side behaviors that user CLAUDE.md rules did not catch: treating absence from search results as evidence of absence, and substituting structure for substance when challenged. It was closed today.
  2. #18435 — Multiple Claude accounts in Claude Desktop with easy profile switching (OPEN, 244 comments, 👍 1032). This is the highest-voted request in the batch. It is a long-running demand from people who split work and personal accounts.
  3. #97074 — Headless claude -p (sdk-cli) uses ~1.8× more of the 5-hour window per token than interactive cli (OPEN, 74 comments, 👍 164). It has a reproduction and affects anyone running CI or automation on a subscription plan. It is a cost-transparency concern.
  4. #69044 — Recurring errors documented over months of daily use (OPEN, 135 comments). It is a structured long-term feedback document, written in German, about reliability and model behavior.
  5. #83033 — Sonnet 5 writes Korean tool-call parameters as \uXXXX escapes and mis-spells the hex (OPEN, 👍 137). It gives a root-cause analysis for Hangul corruption in AskUserQuestion and TodoWrite, and links the earlier reports #80009 and #78996. It is a significant i18n correctness bug.
  6. #24798 — Inter-session communication for multi-Claude workflows (CLOSED, 85 comments). It asked for direct messaging between parallel sessions. The related #86059 reports that the receiving session is interrupted by a cross-session message and then has no memory of it.
  7. #11678 — claude -p fails with tools.3.custom.input_examples: Extra inputs are not permitted (OPEN, 52 comments). It is an API 400 in headless mode, apparently tied to a proxy or gateway setup. It has been open since November 2025.
  8. #25128 — Drag and drop not working in the VS Code extension chat panel (OPEN, 40 comments, 👍 63). It is a regression since about v2.1.6 that still reproduces on macOS. Related: #93782, a 2.1.269 regression where dictation-tool paste fails in the WSL2 VS Code terminal.
  9. #63930 — Prompt cache fully re-created after turns with many parallel tool calls (CLOSED). About 74% of cache writes were wasted on Opus 4.8. Related quota-accounting reports are #81234 and #91775 (the /usage Stats tab inflates totals by about 2×).
  10. #76694 — Cowork: new projects lost "Choose a folder" after the Chat/Cowork merge (OPEN, 41 comments, 👍 30). It is a UX regression from the product merge. Related: #56089, a request to configure the Cowork VM bundle (vhdx) location on Windows (👍 62).

Key PR Progress

No pull requests were updated in the last 24 hours, so there is nothing to report.

Feature Request Trends

  • Multi-account and profile management. #18435 is the clear leader.
  • Multi-session coordination. Users want inter-session messaging and sturdier agent handoffs (#24798, #86059).
  • Context and memory control. One example is excluding parent CLAUDE.md files from auto-loading (#20880). Auto-memory also behaves inconsistently in git worktrees (#81833, #78569).
  • Theming. Requests include themeable inline-code color (#73837).
  • Mobile Remote Control. Prompt suggestions are not displayed (#97410).
  • Cowork configuration. Users want to choose the VM storage location and the project folder (#56089, #76694).

Developer Pain Points

  • Opaque quota and cost metering. Headless runs are charged more than interactive ones. Cache invalidation burns tokens, and /usage over-counts. Weekly quota drains faster than expected (#97074, #63930, #91775, #81234).
  • Billing and support dead ends. Plan upgrades fail, and users report no route to a human (#56281, #68429).
  • Model behavior drift. Reports describe unrequested actions, overconfident claims and unprompted navigation (#60705, #79596).
  • Non-English text corruption in tool calls (#83033).
  • IDE and terminal regressions. These cover VS Code drag and drop, WSL paste, and a Windows BSD0x139 crash in a VS Code session (#25128, #93782, #80912).
  • Auth and connectivity fragility. Short-lived commands abandon OAuth refreshes and leave a spent refresh token (#95822). Persistent ECONNRESET errors on Windows (#85979).
  • Desktop session persistence. Sessions vanish from the UI after a restart (#59736).

Note: Many of today's "updated" items are old issues closed by stale-bot triage, so the update timestamps overstate the amount of fresh activity.

OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode

OpenCode Community Digest: 2026-11-12

1. Today's Highlights

The free-tier megathread (#59387) is still the most active discussion at 360 comments. V2 stability is the other big theme: plugin reloads dropping agents, MCP servers that never retry, and TUI regressions. On the PR side, contributors are fixing core and plugin robustness, SSH recovery and Windows/PowerShell parsing. There is also an experimental native CLI port (#63477).

2. Releases

  • process-daemon-v0.5.2: opencode-pty 0.5.2 (protocol 8), published to npm as @opencode/pty@0.5.2. The notes list no other changes. (anomalyco/opencode, packages/process-daemon)

3. Hot Issues

  1. #59387 Free tier issues megathread. 360 comments, 27 👍. It collects "Free usage exceeded" errors and resets that never happen. It is the biggest support burden right now.
  2. #4283 Copy to clipboard not working (closed). 160 comments, 135 👍. A long-running pain point, now closed after a year.
  3. #2242 Sandboxing the agent. 114 comments, 84 👍. Users want seatbelt-style filesystem restriction like Gemini CLI and Codex. It is still open and a security priority for many.
  4. #45278 Payment declined after 3 months. 44 comments, 36 👍. Billing reliability complaint, now closed.
  5. #12472 Native Claude Code hooks compatibility (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop). 42 👍. It would extend the existing CLAUDE.md and skills compatibility.
  6. #52237 Remote MCP servers that fail once are never retried. After a macOS sleep/wake the service keeps the server in failed state until restart. This hurts MCP reliability.
  7. #49982 Failed plugin reload silently drops custom agents and commands. Now closed. PR #63548 targets it.
  8. #62002 default_agent reverts to build on a hot config reload. Closed. It is likely related to the same reload fragility as #49982.
  9. #63550 Context polluted by another project's content (DeepSeek). It is marked high severity. The user received unrelated Python/FastAPI audit output in a C project. This may be a provider-side leak, and it is closed.
  10. #59461 Desktop crash on startup (SSE4.2 missing). The new Bun runtime needs SSE4.2, so older CPUs crash with error 134. It is still open.

Also worth noting: #48826 (V2 subagents marked completed while background work is pending) and #52941 (desktop file tree shows stale contents after agent edits).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #63477 cli: port to native. A preview of a native CLI, linked to simonklee/opencode-native-preview.
  2. #62743 Connect model providers over a Unix socket. It lets local servers such as llama.cpp, Ollama and vLLM be reached without a socat TCP bridge.
  3. #63548 Keep plugin swaps going when a cleanup fails. It closes #49982 and was closed today, so check whether it landed or was superseded.
  4. #63558 / #63554 Detect PowerShell sl alias in ShellParse. It closes #63551 and fixes directory extraction for Windows. #63554 was closed and #63558 is the open resubmission.
  5. #63542 Recover when the remote SSH service port is taken. It fixes reconnect failures after a dropped connection.
  6. #63544 Advance SSH prompts and close the dialog on connection. It also adds Component Lab flows for QR pairing and password fallback.
  7. #60659 Estimate spend in the TUI mini footer. It is stacked on #59864.
  8. #63553 Worktree badges in the sidebar. Sessions from git worktrees become distinguishable.
  9. #63322 Scroll the always-allow pattern list. It fixes content being clipped by the 15-row permission prompt cap.
  10. #63538 Update e2e specs for always-background subagents. It was closed. Seven app e2e cases had been failing on dev since subagents began always running in the background (#63382, #63391).

5. Feature Request Trends

  • Plugin extensibility on V2: a composer API (#51209), assistant text transforms (#53019) and reactive external TSX plugins (#39986).
  • Ecosystem and distribution: a plugin/agent/skills marketplace (#28696, 38 👍) and Claude Code hooks compatibility (#12472).
  • Security: agent sandboxing (#2242).
  • Workflow and UI: keeping the tab's model across plan/build switches (#54375), web UI project auto-sync (#13626) and a V2 provider catalog reconciled with /models (#40524).

6. Developer Pain Points

  • V2 config and plugin reload fragility: agents and commands are silently lost or reverted (#49982, #62002).
  • Service and connection resilience: MCP servers are not retried (#52237), the client shows a reconnect splash about every 10s (#63417), and SSH reconnects fail.
  • TUI and desktop regressions: the plan-mode reminder persists (#62797), /compact is missing in 2.0.18 (#51638), the file tree is stale (#52941), background shell notices pile up (#63345) and unicode escapes leak into text (#63186).
  • Free tier, billing and provider confusion: usage limits (#59387), declined payments (#45278) and Console/Go provider visibility (#63296).
  • Platform compatibility: SSE4.2 CPU crashes (#59461), Windows desktop tab issues (#63229) and PowerShell parsing.
  • Trust: possible cross-context leakage (#63550) and no built-in sandbox (#2242).

This digest is auto-generated by agents-radar.

item.content:encoded:
MCP Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-12

Issues: 16 | PRs: 11 | Projects covered: 7 | Generated: 2026-11-12 15:44 UTC

  • MCP Servers
  • MCP Registry (official)
  • Awesome MCP Servers
  • Docker MCP Registry
  • Claude Plugins (official)
  • Awesome Claude Code
  • Awesome Agent Skills

MCP Deep Dive

MCP Servers Digest — 2026-11-12

1. Today's Overview

Activity was high and almost entirely maintainer-driven. 16 issues and 11 PRs were updated in 24 hours, and 10 of those 11 PRs were merged or closed. Most were filed and resolved the same day by cliffhall, so the v2 milestone looks like it is in a fast hardening and cleanup phase. The headline change is Streamable HTTP for all reference servers. No new releases shipped, but a Changesets "version packages" PR is open (#5537), so a release looks close.

2. Releases

No new releases today. #5537 (chore: version packages) is open and would publish the pending changesets once merged.

3. Project Progress

Features

  • #5536: Streamable HTTP now served from every reference server. Until now only everything supported it. filesystem, memory and sequentialthinking use the SDK's createMcpHandler. It closes #576, a request open since Jan 2025 with 10 👍.
  • #5534: memory server gets opt-in write limits (MEMORY_MAX_ENTITIES, MEMORY_MAX_RELATIONS, MEMORY_MAX_FILE_BYTES) and documents the linear per-write cost. Closes #5525.

Fixes

  • #5533: git_remote now redacts query values and fragments in URLs, not only userinfo. Closes #5508.
  • #5530: memory server releases lock files on exit and on SIGINT/SIGTERM. Closes #5485.
  • #5535: sequentialthinking counts header rows toward the log box's row cap. Closes #5526.

Docs and CI

  • #5532: everything README now states the whole-segment rule for get-env masking.
  • #5531: stale --db-path comments removed from the fetch and git Dockerfiles.
  • #5529: Dependabot sweep script scopes a hoisted npm copy by the ranges it satisfies.
  • #5528: mcp-interface-diff.yml added as a dispatch-only placeholder (staged rename, step 1).
  • #4528: CI that auto-closes new-server PRs and triages new-server issues. It enforces the policy that new servers belong in the Registry.

4. Community Hot Topics

  • #5508 (6 comments): credential redaction in git_remote. Users expect the documented "redacted" promise to cover every part of a URL.
  • #5483 (4 comments): stale Docker comments. This is a docs-quality signal from an external contributor.
  • #3047 (4 comments, 3 👍): registering the reference servers in the official Registry. It is part of the move away from the old reference-server model.
  • #576 (10 👍, the most reactions): demand for Streamable HTTP. It is now resolved.
  • #5485 (3 comments) and #5260 (3 comments): lock-file hygiene and Windows filesystem safety.

The underlying needs are reliable remote transport, safe handling of secrets, and clean shutdown behavior.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

  1. Security, open: #5260 — filesystem parent-directory swap on Windows. This is a follow-up to GHSA-53mr-w429-c597. The earlier fix covers only Linux and macOS. No fix PR yet.
  2. Security, open: #5520 — git should refuse a Windows junction that leads outside --repository. It is a follow-up to GHSA-q74p-4wrc-q7w6, which was fixed in 2026.11.11. No fix PR yet.
  3. Security, fixed: #5508 — credential leak through URL query or fragment. Fixed by #5533.
  4. Stability, fixed: #5485 — stale lock files after a signal. Fixed by #5530.
  5. Low, fixed: #5526 — log-box row cap bypass. Fixed by #5535.
  6. Open, upstream-blocked: #5176 — the string "null" arrives as None in git arguments. It is waiting on python-sdk#3055.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #5538: CORS and preflight handling for the new Streamable HTTP endpoints. This is a likely follow-up, because browser clients on localhost cannot connect without it.
  • #5525: size caps for memory writes, already delivered as opt-in limits. Making them the default may come later.
  • #3047: Registry registration of the reference servers.
  • CI and tooling: the staged workflow rename (#5527, step 2) and a GitHub App for board writes (#5061).

The next release will likely include Streamable HTTP, the memory limits and the security fixes, with CORS shortly after.

7. User Feedback Summary

Few reports came from outside the maintainers. reservoir-cmyk filed three reports (#5524, #5525, #5526), and each was closed the same day. The reports point to these pain points:

  • Documentation that does not match the code's behavior.
  • Missing resource limits.
  • Unclean process shutdown. The memory server report came from a Claude Desktop and agent-orchestrator setup.
  • Servers that cannot be reached over HTTP.

Turnaround on external reports is excellent.

8. Backlog Watch

  • #3047: the Registry tracking issue, open since 2025-11-23, a full year.
  • #5176: open since 2026-10-19 and blocked on the Python SDK. It needs upstream attention.
  • #5260: a Windows security gap open since 2026-10-25.
  • #5061: the board-automation GitHub App, open since 2026-10-07.
  • #5537: the release PR needs a maintainer to merge it.

Project health: strong. Resolution is fast and security follow-ups are tracked openly. The main risks are the two open Windows path-safety issues and the CORS gap in the new HTTP endpoints.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report: MCP and Agent-Tooling Ecosystem, 2026-11-12

1. Ecosystem Overview

The projects covered are mostly not agents. They are the infrastructure and distribution layer around agents: reference MCP servers, the official registry, catalogs (Awesome MCP, Docker MCP Registry, Awesome Claude Code, Awesome Agent Skills), and the official Claude plugin directory. Almost all of the activity is inbound submissions: 141 PRs on Awesome MCP, 50 on Docker MCP Registry and 24 submission issues on Awesome Claude Code. Maintainer capacity is the common constraint. Three themes recur across projects: remote and hosted servers with OAuth, agent memory and context, and security hardening. This points to a move from "build a server" to "distribute, verify and trust a server."

2. Activity Comparison

Health scores are my own judgment from the digests, not figures the digests report.

Project Issues updated PRs updated Release status Health (1–5) Note
MCP Servers 16 11 (10 merged/closed) None; release PR #5537 open 4.5 Fast, maintainer-driven resolution
MCP Registry 3 4 (all closed/merged) None 4 Clear queue; #1819 stale-data bug and a 19 Nov deadline (#1778)
Awesome MCP Servers 0 141 (127 open) None 3 High volume; review comments and merge detail not visible
Docker MCP Registry 1 50 (49 open, 1 closed) None 2.5 Review throughput is the bottleneck; backlog of weeks
Claude Plugins (official) 3 27 (16 closed/merged) None; security-guidance 2.0.20 staged (#7094) 4 Responsive on security; the Verified-org policy is unclear (#7024, 26 comments)
Awesome Claude Code 24 0 None 3.5 Healthy intake; no visible curation (19 awaiting)
Awesome Agent Skills 0 6 (5 open, 1 closed) None 3 Low engagement; some review lag

3. MCP Servers's Position

Advantages

  • Resolution speed. 10 of 11 PRs were closed or merged within the window. Docker MCP Registry closed 1 of 50, and Awesome MCP closed 14 of 141.
  • Issue-to-fix pipeline. External reports were fixed the same day (#5508, #5485, #5526), and security follow-ups are tracked openly.
  • Spec-level role. It is the reference implementation that the other projects list or package. Streamable HTTP now covers every reference server (#5536).

Technical approach differences

  • It ships code (TypeScript and Python servers, SDK handlers). The Registry, Docker registry and Awesome lists ship metadata about other people's code.
  • It has stopped accepting new third-party servers (#4528 auto-closes them) and sends them to the Registry. That makes it the reference and the Registry the discovery layer.
  • Security work is at the code level (path safety, redaction, lock files), where the Claude Plugins work is at the policy and hook level.

Community size

  • By raw volume it is mid-sized: 27 items updated, against 141 PRs for Awesome MCP and 50 for Docker.
  • It has the highest share of resolved work and the lowest external contribution. Most activity is from one maintainer (cliffhall), which is a concentration risk.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Need Projects Specifics
Remote and hosted servers, OAuth MCP Servers, Docker MCP Registry, Awesome MCP Streamable HTTP (#5536); OAuth 2.1/PKCE/DCR submissions (#6999, #5541); CORS gap (#5538); hosted servers growing on Awesome MCP
Security and supply chain Servers, Registry, Plugins, Agent Skills Windows path safety (#5260, #5520); namespace takeover on domain change (#1778); Verified-org gating (#7024); ReDoS and bare-repo hardening (#7070, #7093); MCP rug-pull defense (#1398)
Agent memory and context Servers, Awesome MCP, Awesome Claude Code Memory write limits (#5534); Firekeep and Zenod; Agent Journal and Deiko; cross-agent sharing across Claude Code, Codex and others
Discovery and metadata quality Registry, Awesome lists, Docker Description search (#1850); Glama, naming and emoji checks; empty tools.json with dynamic discovery
Cross-agent interoperability Awesome MCP, Awesome Claude Code, Agent Skills Claude Code with Codex, Cursor and pi; npx skills add
Review automation Awesome MCP, Docker, Awesome Claude Code, Plugins Label checks, validation bots, CI on SHA bumps. Auto-closes of pending items (Awesome Claude Code) lose some submissions
Cost and usage visibility Awesome Claude Code Four monitoring submissions (usage menu bar apps, GNOME extension)

5. Differentiation Analysis

Project Focus Primary users Architecture and gate
MCP Servers Reference implementations Server authors, SDK users Code monorepo; maintainer-gated; new servers redirected
MCP Registry Canonical discovery and publishing Publishers, clients API service (/v0/servers); namespace verified by domain
Awesome MCP Curated list Developers browsing Markdown PRs; Glama listing and bot labels required
Docker MCP Registry Packaged and remote catalog Docker Desktop users, vendors Config PRs; increasingly listing-only remote entries
Claude Plugins (official) First-party plugin directory and security plugin Claude Code users, plugin authors Pinned SHAs; Verified-org rule for hooks and local MCP; CI validation
Awesome Claude Code Claude Code resources Claude Code power users Issue-form submissions with bot validation
Awesome Agent Skills Skills catalog Cross-agent skill users PR list; narrower scope

The main split is gatekeeping model. The Registry and the Plugins directory verify identity (domain, Verified org). The Awesome lists and Docker mainly check format and rely on volunteers for judgement. This difference decides how much supply-chain risk each channel carries.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

  • Tier 1, very high intake: Awesome MCP (141 PRs), Docker MCP Registry (50), Awesome Claude Code (24 new issues). Demand outruns review, so these are scaling, not stabilizing.
  • Tier 2, rapid iteration with strong delivery: MCP Servers (v2 hardening, release PR open) and Claude Plugins (security-guidance 2.0.20 staged). Both are releasing soon.
  • Tier 3, stabilizing: MCP Registry. Its queue is clear and its issues are few. The open risks are #1819 and the 19 Nov namespace deadline.
  • Tier 4, low engagement: Awesome Agent Skills, with 6 PRs, no comments and a month-long review lag.

No project shipped a release today. Two are one merge away from one: MCP Servers and the security-guidance plugin.

7. Trend Signals

  1. Remote MCP is becoming the default. Reference servers now serve Streamable HTTP, and Docker submissions are mostly hosted with OAuth. Developers should plan for OAuth 2.1 with DCR and for CORS. The CORS issue (#5538) shows browser clients are not yet covered.
  2. Trust is the bottleneck, more than supply. There are many submissions and little verification. Verified-org gating, namespace locking and tool-surface freezing (#1398) all point the same way. Pin versions and check publisher identity before depending on a server.
  3. Windows parity gaps. Open path-safety issues (#5260, #5520) and the PowerShell commit-review fix (#7076) show security tooling was built first for Linux and macOS.
  4. Memory is a crowded, unsettled category. It appears in the reference server, the Awesome lists and the Claude Code resource list. Cross-agent portability is the differentiator to watch. Resource limits (#5534) suggest unbounded stores cause real problems.
  5. Dynamic tool discovery conflicts with static catalogs. Empty tools.json entries in Docker's registry show that catalog schemas have not caught up with servers that list tools at runtime.
  6. Agent output verification. Stop-hook claim checks and policy layers appear in the Awesome Claude Code submissions. This is an early signal of demand for guardrails on agent claims.
  7. Maintainer review capacity is the scaling limit. Agent-authored PRs (the 🤖 labels on Awesome MCP) raise submission volume faster than review can grow. Expect more automated gating and disclosure rules.

Caveats. Several digests lack comment counts and merge-versus-close detail (Awesome MCP, Docker, Agent Skills). Health scores and activity tiers are inferred from a single day's data, and they reflect that day only.

Peer Project Reports

MCP Registry (official) — modelcontextprotocol/registry

MCP Registry Digest — 2026-11-12

1. Today's Overview

Activity in modelcontextprotocol/registry was light: 3 issues and 4 PRs were updated, with no new releases. All 4 PRs were closed or merged and none remain open, so the PR queue is clear. Two of the three issues are still open, and one is time-sensitive (a namespace lock deadline on 19 Nov). Overall health looks stable, with maintainers triaging quickly. One fix landed for a user-reported search gap.

2. Releases

No new releases.

3. Project Progress

Four PRs were closed or merged. The summaries don't say which were merged and which were closed unmerged, so the status of each is noted as given.

  • Search fix: PR #1850 "fix(search): match server descriptions in registry search". It fixes #1807. Before this, GET /v0/servers?search=… matched only server_name. Terms that appeared only in a description never returned the server. Issue #1807 was closed the same day.
  • UI: PR #1573 "fix(ui): prefer human-readable server title in registry cards". It makes the optional server.title the primary card heading and keeps server.name as a smaller secondary label. It was opened on 2026-08-25 and closed after about 11 weeks.
  • Dependencies: Dependabot PRs #1853 (GitHub Actions group: pulumi/actions 7.0.0→7.1.0, docker/login-action, sigstore/cosign-installer) and #1852 (deploy Go dependencies: pulumi-kubernetes sdk and pulumi sdk). Both are routine maintenance.

4. Community Hot Topics

Comment volume is low, so there is no strong hotspot.

  • #1778 (4 comments, the most active): the publisher of com.getmattered/getmattered asks to lock the com.aiapplyd namespace. The domain that verifies it changes owner on 19 Nov 2026. Underlying need: a way to retire or protect namespaces whose domain ownership is changing. Without one, a new domain owner could take over the old namespace and publish under it, which is a supply-chain risk. Versions 1.6.0–1.9.0 are already deprecated.
  • #1807 (1 comment): the need for better discovery as the registry grows. Users want to find servers by function, not just by name.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

  1. #1819, open, no fix PR. The status update succeeds, but the list endpoint keeps returning stale duplicate rows. Repro: publish the same version (0.7.16) twice on different days, then publish 0.7.17. GET /v0/servers?search=... then returns both 0.7.16 rows with active/isLatest flags still set. This is a data-consistency problem that can mislead clients about which version is current.
  2. #1807, closed. Search ignored descriptions. It was fixed by PR #1850.

No crashes or outages were reported.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Namespace locking or retirement (#1778). This has a hard deadline and could be handled manually by maintainers, but it points to a missing feature: handling domain ownership changes systematically.
  • Description search is already fixed in the API (#1850) and will likely appear in the next release.
  • Human-readable titles in cards (#1573) was closed. The summary doesn't say whether it was merged, so it is unclear whether it will ship.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Users struggle to discover servers unless they already know the exact name. This is the clearest pain point today.
  • Publishers worry about identity and namespace security when domains change hands.
  • Publishers who correct metadata by re-publishing run into version-state inconsistencies.
  • Response times are good. Search issue #1807 went from report (11-06) to fix (11-11) and closure (11-12) in about 6 days.

8. Backlog Watch

  • #1778 needs maintainer action before 19 Nov 2026, about 7 days from today. It has been open since 2026-10-31 with no recorded resolution.
  • #1819 is open with no fix PR and only 1 comment. It deserves triage because of its effect on version correctness.
  • PR #1573 sat for about 11 weeks before being closed. This suggests contributor PRs on UI work can wait a long time for review.
Awesome MCP Servers — punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers

Awesome MCP Servers Digest — 2026-11-12

Source: punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers

The repo is a curated list, so activity is almost entirely submission PRs. In the last 24h, 141 PRs were updated (127 open, 14 merged/closed). There were no issues and no releases. Docker MCP Registry — docker/mcp-registry

Docker MCP Registry Digest, 2026-11-12

1. Today's Overview

The registry is very active but almost entirely on the intake side. 50 PRs were updated in 24h (49 open, 1 merged/closed) against 1 updated issue, and there were no releases. Nearly every PR is a new remote (hosted, listing-only) server submission. Several were opened today (#6997–#7011), which suggests steady inbound volume. Throughput is the weak spot. No new releases.

3. Project Progress

Only 1 PR was merged or closed in the window, and the data doesn't say which one. No feature or fix progress can be attributed to it. The merge-to-submission ratio today is about 1:49.

4. Community Hot Topics

Comment counts are reported as undefined and reactions are 0 everywhere, so no item stands out on engagement. The data shows these themes:

  • Remote and OAuth servers are the norm. Examples are #6600 Aithon (Streamable HTTP, bearer key for orders), #5541 TestMu AI (OAuth with dynamic client registration), #6999 BillDog (OAuth 2.1, PKCE, DCR), #7002 Post Reef and #7009 Suelomio.   • Several entries ship an empty tools.json with dynamic tool discovery (e.g. #7000, #7005). Handling of this pattern will likely need to be settled in review guidance.
  • Likely near-term outcome: the simplest remote entries (public, unauthenticated, such as #7008 HolicAudit) are the easiest to approve.

7. User Feedback Summary

There are no comments or reactions, so direct feedback is absent. The submissions imply these needs:

  • Clear guidance on OAuth, test credentials and dynamic tool lists.
  • Visibility for commercial services in the Docker catalog.

All were updated today, probably through bot or CI activity, but none has a visible review outcome. The 49 open PRs against 1 close or merge in the window point to a growing queue. Triage automation or batch review of remote-only entries would help.

Claude Plugins (official) — anthropics/claude-plugins-official

Claude Plugins (Official) Digest — 2026-11-12

Repo: anthropics/claude-plugins-official

1. Today's Overview

Activity is high. 27 PRs and 3 issues were updated in 24 hours, with no new releases. Most of the work is the security-guidance plugin hardening series from maintainer mhegazy, plus the automated SHA-bump stream from github-actions[bot]. The most active discussion is a community thread on organization verification, which blocks plugin submissions. CI and submission-flow tooling were also reworked today.

2. Releases

None. security-guidance 2.0.20 is staged in open PR #7094, pending #7092 and #7093.

3. Project Progress

Of the 27 PRs, 16 were merged or closed and 11 remain open.

security-guidance hardening (closed or merged):

  • #7076: reviews commits and pushes made via the PowerShell tool. Fixes #7005.
  • #7072: reviews extra commits sent by a combined commit-and-push command.
  • #7081: takes the review model from one place and defaults to the newest listed.
  • #7073: requires the pip temp folder to be a real, user-owned folder (0700).
  • #7070: stops custom-rule regexes from running too long (ReDoS). A pattern like (a+){2,}$ took 8.5 s on 28 characters.
  • #7055: custom rule globs can be relative to the project.
  • #7054: reads yaml.load, torch.load and np.load calls across their arguments.

Directory and CI:

  • #7086 and #7085: CI now validates in-repo plugin folders, fixes the frontmatter check, and points submissions to claude.ai/directory/manage.
  • #7084: claude-for-manufacturing plugin proposal, closed.
  • #6338: Xcode plugin, closed. It carried over #6259 so its checks could run.

Still open:

  • security-guidance: #7092 (records and markers opened through one helper) and #7093 (git runs only in ordinary checkouts, with safe.bareRepository=explicit).
  • Automated SHA bumps: #7087–#7091 (blackrock-advisor-center, cloudinary, growthbook, rootly, streaming-skills) and #6451 (data-agent-kit).

4. Community Hot Topics

  • #7024, "How can an organization become Verified?" has 26 comments and 9 👍, the most of any item. Since about 2026-11-05 the directory rejects command hooks and local MCP servers from non-Verified organizations. The need is a documented, transparent path to Verified status. The reporter says the pre-submission docs don't explain it. This is the main friction point for third-party plugin authors.
  • The security-guidance PR series (#7054, #7055, #7070) has no comments. It references claude-code issues #99553, #86545 and #98547, so the work is driven by user reports upstream.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

  1. Merge-commit push review re-reports old findings: #7043 (closed). _compute_push_sweep_base diffs from the merged-in parent's lineage, so it reviews that branch's whole divergence. The result is noisy, misleading reviews. No linked fix PR appears in today's data. The closure suggests it was resolved, but I can't confirm that from this data.
  2. Silent skip of PowerShell commits on Windows: #7005 (closed). Commits and pushes went unreviewed with no message to the user, which is a security gap. Fixed by #7076.
  3. Hardening items: ReDoS in custom regexes (#7070), pip temp folder ownership (#7073), and file/marker handling and bare-repo safety (#7092, #7093). The last two are still open.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • A clear Verified-organization path (#7024). The directory's submission link moved to claude.ai/directory/manage in #7085/#7086, which suggests a submission-flow overhaul is underway. Updated documentation is likely.
  • security-guidance 2.0.20 (#7094) is the most likely next release. It was tested on Linux, macOS and Windows and is waiting on #7092 and #7093.
  • Directory growth: Xcode and manufacturing plugin submissions were closed today.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Plugin authors: frustration over the sudden Verified-only restriction on command hooks and local MCP servers. The docs lag the enforcement, and the date of the change is not clearly announced.
  • Windows users: expect parity in security tooling across shells, such as PowerShell.
  • Security-guidance users: want accurate, low-noise reviews (no re-reporting after merges) and more reliable custom rules (relative globs, safe regexes).

8. Backlog Watch

  • #6451: the data-agent-kit SHA bump has been open since 2026-10-11, about a month. Newer bump PRs opened the same day are also waiting. It may be stuck and needs a maintainer to check.
  • #7024: it is open with 26 comments and needs an authoritative maintainer answer on Verified criteria and process.
  • The open SHA-bump PRs (#7087–#7091) have no review activity yet. Confirm they are auto-merged or reviewed on a regular schedule.

Project health: high throughput, with a responsive maintainer on security fixes. The main risk is the lack of communication around Verified-org policy.

Awesome Claude Code — hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code

Awesome Claude Code Digest — 2026-11-12

1. Today's Overview

Activity today is almost entirely inbound resource submissions. 24 issues were updated, and 0 PRs and 0 releases were recorded. 19 issues are open and 5 are closed. Of the 5 closed issues, 3 were auto-closed because validation was still pending and 1 failed validation. The fifth is #3221, which carries both passed and failed labels. Submission volume is high: 22 of the 24 updated issues were created on 11-11 or 11-12. Nearly all have a single bot comment, so the validation pipeline is running. No human maintainer activity is visible in the data, and the PR queue is empty.

2. Releases

No new releases.

3. Project Progress

No PRs were merged or closed in the last 24h. The only visible progress is on the intake side:

  • 19 submissions are marked validation-passed and wait for maintainer curation.
  • #3221 Quick Actions (Mods) is closed. It was created 2026-10-23, so it was touched today after about 3 weeks. Its labels show both validation-passed and validation-failed. This suggests it was re-validated or its status changed.

4. Community Hot Topics

No issue has more than 2 comments, and none has reactions. The one with 2 comments is #3221. All other issues have 1 comment (the validation bot) or 0. The signal is therefore in submission themes rather than discussion:

  • Usage and cost monitoring (4 submissions, a notable cluster): TokenPlant #3642, Tripmeter #3640, Usagebar #3637. Two of these are macOS menu bar apps and one is a GNOME extension. The need is visibility into Claude Code usage limits.
  • Memory and context persistence (4): Agent Journal #3636, picture-diary #3627, Dawnmere #3624, Deiko #3619. Several are cross-agent (Claude Code, Codex, pi).
  • Multi-agent and orchestration: spec-first #3644, crosscheck #3632 (Claude Code and Codex as mutual reviewers), Airone Giallo #3634.
  • Safety and verification: aiZee #3641 (a policy layer) and claim-check #3629 (a Stop hook that verifies "fixed" and "tests pass" claims).

5. Bugs & Stability

No bugs, crashes, or regressions were reported, and there are no fix PRs. The only stability-related items concern the intake workflow:

  • #3628 Tisty failed validation and was closed. Its summary is empty, so the body may be malformed or missing the template.
  • #3635 Nexity, #3621 Files pane and #3620 claude-code-video-studio were auto-closed while validation-pending. Possible causes are a validation timeout or a failed check. Submitters may need to resubmit.
  • Some titles lack the [Resource]: prefix (#3641, #3632, #3628, #3619). These issues still passed validation, apart from #3628.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

There are no explicit feature requests. The category mix points to where the ecosystem is growing:

  • Observability and cost tracking is the strongest cluster. A dedicated "Usage & Cost" subcategory already exists and is getting traffic.
  • Cross-agent interoperability (Claude Code with Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Devin, pi) appears in #3632, #3636, #3641 and #3633.
  • Other categories seeing submissions are Infrastructure and DevOps (#3643), Providers and Runtime (#3638 UEAgent), Creative Media (#3639 Klad), Testing, Configuration (#3631) and Documentation and Learning (#3630).
  • Expect the next list update to add entries in these categories. Usage & Cost is likely to grow the most.

7. User Feedback Summary

Contributors are not reporting pain directly, but their projects show it:

  • Users want visibility into rate and usage limits (menu bar and shell widgets).
  • Agents lose state between sessions and across tools, which drives the memory and journal projects.
  • There is a trust gap in agent output ("fixed", "tests pass"), which motivates claim-check and aiZee.
  • Users run several accounts or agents and need to bridge them (#3631).
  • Some auto-closures may frustrate submitters who get no clear reason.

8. Backlog Watch

The data covers only 24h of updates, so older backlog cannot be assessed fully. Items needing maintainer attention:

  • 19 open validation-passed submissions (#3619 to #3644) are awaiting curation. This is a large single-day batch.
  • #3221 Quick Actions, open since 2026-10-23, shows conflicting validation labels. A maintainer should confirm whether it should be listed.
  • Auto-closed submissions (#3635, #3621, #3620) may need a clearer resubmission path.
  • #3638 UEAgent has 0 comments, unlike the others. The bot may have missed it, so it is worth checking.

Health assessment: Intake is healthy and submissions are strong. Curation throughput, with no PRs and no releases, is the likely bottleneck.

Awesome Agent Skills — VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills

Awesome Agent Skills Digest — 2026-11-12

1. Today's Overview

The project is a curated catalog with no code or releases, so activity shows up almost entirely as community submission PRs. In the last 24h there were 0 issues and 6 PRs updated (5 open, 1 closed). Four of the PRs were opened on 11-11 or 11-12, which indicates steady inbound submission volume. No PR has comments or reactions, and none was merged today. Activity is healthy on the intake side, but review and merge throughput is unclear.

2. Releases

None.

3. Project Progress

No PRs were merged today. One was closed:

  • #1182 — hunxuankai/wxpusher-integration (WxPusher notification integration, Productivity and Collaboration). It was opened on 2026-10-10 and closed on 11-12 after about a month. The data does not say whether it was rejected or superseded, so the reason is unknown.

4. Community Hot Topics

No item has comments or 👍 reactions, so there are no hot topics by engagement. By submission themes, today's new PRs cluster as follows:

  • Security and integrity: #1398 mcp-surface-integrity freezes an MCP server's tool surface and verifies it on each call, to catch rug-pull-style changes. This reflects growing demand for MCP supply-chain safeguards.
  • Marketing and SEO: #1394 Illyism/seo-skills is a bundle of 17 SEO skills from a repo with 890+ stars.
  • Specialized domains: #1397 adds three skills (klad, klad-drawing, klad-pixel).

  • Off-scope: #1395 "Claude to PDF" is a Chrome extension, not a skill, so it likely doesn't fit the list's criteria.

5. Bugs & Stability

No bugs, crashes, or regressions were reported. There were no issues, and no fix PRs.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

No explicit feature requests were filed. Implicit signals from the submissions:

  • Demand for security-oriented skills for MCP and agents (#1398).
  • Growth in domain-specific skills and multi-skill bundles (#1397, #1394).
  • Submitters are targeting existing categories (Development and Testing, Marketing, Specialized Domains), so the taxonomy appears adequate. Nothing here suggests a structural change.

7. User Feedback Summary

There is no direct feedback today. Submission patterns show that contributors value inclusion in the list as a discovery channel. Install commands such as npx skills add and MIT licensing are highlighted in the submissions. One submitter (#1395) appears to have misread the list's scope, so the contribution guidelines may need clearer wording on what counts as a skill.

8. Backlog Watch

  • The #1182 closure shows a roughly one-month turnaround on an older submission, which suggests some review lag.
  • The PR numbers range up to #1398, while this window shows only 5 open PRs, all from the last two days. The data does not cover older open PRs, so the full backlog size can't be assessed. Maintainers should check for older unreviewed submissions.
  • #1395 likely needs a quick scope-based close or redirect.
  • Security-relevant #1398 merits a careful review before listing.

Project health: Intake is strong, and engagement and visible merge activity are low today.

AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-11-12

Generated: 2026-11-12 15:44 UTC | Projects covered: 2

  • Dify
  • LiteLLM

Cross-Project Comparison

AI Infrastructure Cross-Project Comparison, 2026-11-12

Scope: Only two digests were provided: Dify (LLM app platform) and LiteLLM (LLM gateway). No inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama) or fine-tuning projects (Unsloth) were included. Sections 3 and 4 are therefore limited, and I note where I can't draw conclusions.

1. Ecosystem Overview

Today's activity sits in the application and gateway layers, not the engine layer. LiteLLM shipped four releases across four release lines (v1.110.0-rc.2, v1.109.1, v1.108.6 LTS, v1.106.9). Dify shipped none. Both projects spent the day on correctness: budget and cost accounting, SSE streaming integrity, and version regressions. Both are also adding agent-interoperability surface (Dify's A2A external agents, LiteLLM's Cursor CLI passthrough and LiteFlow workflows). Neither reported a measurable performance gain.

2. Activity Comparison

Counts are the distinct issues and PRs cited in each digest, not repository totals. They indicate relative focus only.

Project Issues cited PRs cited Release status
Dify ~26 (about 8 closed) 9 (6 are test-infrastructure PRs) No release in 24h. Regressions are tied to 1.17.0, 1.18.x and 1.19.0.
LiteLLM ~20 (4 closed, mostly stale cleanup) 13 4 releases: v1.110.0-rc.2, v1.109.1, v1.108.6 (LTS), v1.106.9. Release notes in the data are truncated to the cosign signature header.
  • Dify's PRs: The large feature PRs are #45918 (BYOA/A2A) and #46090 (malware scanning), both XXL.
  • LiteLLM's PRs: These are mostly backports and gateway-feature work.

3. Model Support Race

No new model architectures shipped in either project, so there is no race to rank from this data.

  • LiteLLM is the only one with provider and modality expansion, and all of it is in open PRs and unreleased:
    • Replicate video, image and TTS (#51360).
    • Bedrock s3:// media for image, document and video (#50577, backport #50401).
    • gemini/gemini-decision-1 (#51362).
    • Image support for Perplexity and OpenRouter decision models (#48846, a behavior change for drop_params users).
    • Native Gemini generateContent for custom providers (#51083).
    • An open request for IONOS (#40112).
  • Dify has no model or hardware changes.
  • Gap: There is no hardware-support signal (GPU, NPU, ROCm and so on) from either project. Engine-level model support can't be assessed without the vLLM, SGLang and llama.cpp digests.

4. Performance Frontier

The data has no KV cache, batching, quantization, distributed-serving or kernel work. The only efficiency items are in the gateway and app layers.

  • LiteLLM:
    • #51342 fixes Redis connection leaks in sync run_async_function.
    • #50065 reports that MCP tools/list has blocked for 18–50 s since v1.108.0 on a legacy subscription listener. This is the largest quantified latency problem in the data, and no fix PR is visible.
  • Dify: #46157 reports about 70 GiB of Playwright traces (3,264 files) on a developer machine. It is a dev-environment issue only.

At this layer the bottlenecks are connection management, protocol-handling latency and state accounting, not GPU throughput.

5. Layer Positioning

Layer Project Today's evidence
Application and agent platform Dify Agent v2, workflows, knowledge pipelines, A2A agent calls, and upload security (malware scanning). Consumes models but doesn't serve them.
Gateway and routing LiteLLM Provider normalization, budgets and rate limits, cost tracking, /v1/messages translation, MCP and passthrough. Sits between clients and engines.
Serving engine, local runtime, fine-tuning Not covered No data supplied.

LiteLLM's reasoning-backend issue (#32357) names vLLM and SGLang as upstreams, so engine behavior surfaces through the gateway as translation bugs.

6. Trend Signals

  1. Gateway accounting is the weak point. LiteLLM's top issues are budget bypass (#34238), reservation leaks on stream disconnect (#50534), TPM counters that outlive their window (#49675), and up to 1,000,000× overbilling from unvalidated usage.cost (#48398). Multi-pod Redis deployments carry the most risk.
  2. Streaming and protocol translation is the main source of correctness bugs. This shows up in both projects:
    • Dify: missing tool output in SSE (#46034) and SSE reconnect exhaustion (#46109).
    • LiteLLM: empty content for reasoning models via /v1/messages (#32357) and response.failed returned as HTTP 200 (#36768).
  3. Agent interoperability is expanding. Dify's A2A backend, LiteLLM's Cursor CLI passthrough and LiteFlow workflows, and MCP latency are all agent-protocol work.
  4. Release hygiene. LiteLLM runs parallel LTS and RC lines with backports. Dify's regressions cluster in 1.17–1.19, including RBAC demotion and structured output.
  5. Upload security is emerging. Dify's opt-in malware scanning (#46090) and LiteLLM's spend-log token redaction (#48968) both aim at untrusted input and leaked secrets.

What agent and application developers should do:

  • Add provider-side spend caps and reconcile gateway cost against billing.
  • Test /v1/messages with reasoning backends before relying on it for Claude Code or Anthropic SDK clients.
  • Add client-side fallback polling for long agent runs that exhaust SSE reconnects.
  • Check MCP tools/list latency before moving to LiteLLM 1.108.x or later.
  • Pin Dify versions and test in staging before upgrading from 1.17.x or later.
  • Review the LiteLLM release pages directly, because the changelogs in today's data were truncated.

Per-Project Reports

Dify — langgenius/dify

Dify Digest — 2026-11-12

Note: Dify is an LLM app platform, not an inference engine. The hardware and model sections are mostly empty for that reason.

1. Today's Highlights

No release shipped in the last 24h. Activity centered on three things:

  • A wave of bug reports on Agent v2, Workflow and Knowledge Pipeline, mostly against 1.18/1.19.
  • A large BYOA external-agent (A2A) backend PR.
  • A knowledge-base malware-scanning PR.

Contributors also continued a bulk effort to bring unit tests under strict Pyrefly, and the web team continued migrating tests to Browser Mode.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

No releases in the last 24h. Version-sensitive reports:

  • Knowledge Pipeline upload regression since 1.17.0: #46121
  • AWS S3 datasource bug on v1.19.0: #46112 (closed)
  • Structured output "stage=capability" failure on 1.18.0: #45317 (closed)

3. New Model & Hardware Support

There are no model or hardware changes today. Related feature PRs:

  • #45918 (XXL): External Agents backend (BYOA). A2A endpoints can be verified, saved, tested, and called from Agent v2 Workflow/Chatflow nodes. It includes revision management, and execution persists invocation state before remote I/O.
  • #46090 (XXL): per-knowledge-base malware scanning of uploads. It is off by default and gated by FILE_SCAN_ENABLED=true.

4. Performance & Optimization

No performance work with measurable numbers landed. The one resource-related item:

  • #46157 (closed): local Playwright retain-on-failure traces produced 3,264 files, about 70 GiB, on one developer machine. This affects dev environments only.

Test infrastructure PRs (strict Pyrefly cleanup and Browser Mode migration) are in flight:

  • #46189
  • #46188
  • #46187
  • #46185
  • #46184
  • #46186

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by estimated severity. Fix PRs are not visible in the data unless noted.

High

  1. #46109 (open): an Agent run fails with "SSE stream reconnect attempts exhausted" while still making progress.
  2. #46121 (open): Knowledge Pipeline local-file upload returns 415 for images and PPTX files that the data source node allows. The cause is the ?source=datasets check, and it has been a regression since 1.17.0.
  3. #46034 (open) and #44141 (closed): output from a workflow-as-tool or non-streaming tool variable is missing from the chat-messages SSE stream and from saved answers.
  4. #38867 (closed): the Answer node does not work inside an iteration, and the SSE response has no "message" event.

Medium

  • #46129 (open): Notion indexing fails with "invalid data source field: notion_workspace_id" when the plugin returns an empty workspace_id.
  • #46169 (open): the downstream variable picker hides declared Agent v2 object fields.
  • #46165 (open): Last Run omits Iteration and Loop child logs after single-node debugging.
  • #46162 (open): the web SSE handler leaves the response open after rejecting an event.
  • #46136 (open): the webhook trigger drops the file name and extension on multipart uploads.
  • #46152 (open): serialize_request() drops a trailing ? from the query string.
  • #44961 (closed): with RBAC enabled, resources created by an admin disappear after the admin is demoted to Editor (1.18.0).
  • #45206 (closed): the Agent drops parallel tool calls that share a plugin tool call ID.
  • #46002 (closed): the OAuth proxy context can be consumed more than once concurrently.
  • #37045 (closed): Weaviate BM25 full-text search always drops results because the score is not extracted.
  • #46153 (closed): OpenAPI custom tools get a double slash when servers[0].url ends with /.

Low (UI/UX)

  • #46167: the canvas does not highlight the Human Input timeout branch.
  • #46146: the Marketplace catalog loses keyboard focus when the header hides.
  • #46120: chat history stops above the latest message after Markdown expands.
  • #46088 (closed): the Agent prompt does not update when a referenced skill's display name changes.

Maintenance tracking:

  • #43035: pending dependency upgrades.
  • #45584: use the SQLAlchemy engine.
  • #45166: rewrite a property to take a Session parameter.

Related PR: #43241 lets a required Number input accept 0. Workflow Test Run currently rejects numeric zero.

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Agents and streaming: if you consume chat-messages SSE with workflow-as-tool or non-streaming variables, check that final outputs arrive (#46034). For long agent runs, handle reconnect exhaustion on the client side with a fallback poll of the final result (#46109).
  • Knowledge Pipeline: if you upload images or PPTX through the local-file source on 1.17+, expect 415 errors until #46121 is fixed. Check S3 and Notion datasource credentials and workspace IDs (#46112, #46129).
  • Custom tools and triggers: normalize trailing slashes in OpenAPI server URLs (#46153). Webhook multipart file names may be lost (#46136).
  • Upcoming features: BYOA external agents (#45918) will let you call A2A agents from workflows. Optional malware scanning of knowledge-base uploads (#46090) will be relevant if you accept untrusted files.
  • Upgrades: 1.18.x and 1.19.0 are the source of several regressions in this batch, including RBAC demotion and structured output. Pin versions and test staging before upgrading.
LiteLLM — BerriAI/litellm

LiteLLM Digest — 2026-11-12

1. Today's Highlights

LiteLLM shipped four releases in 24h across multiple release lines: the v1.110.0-rc.2 release candidate, v1.109.1, v1.108.6 (LTS line) and v1.106.9. Active PR work centers on rate-limit and budget correctness (borrowed team shares, streaming-disconnect reservation leaks), Bedrock s3:// media support, and new gateway surface (Replicate media, Cursor CLI passthrough, LiteFlow workflows). Open bugs concentrate on cost and budget accounting and on /v1/messages translation for reasoning models.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

  • v1.110.0-rc.2, v1.109.1, v1.108.6, v1.106.9: The release notes in the data are truncated to the cosign image-signature verification header. All images are signed with the key from commit e82a3c6. I can't report changelog contents, so check the release pages before upgrading.
  • Backports are flowing to the release branches rc/1.109.0 and lts/1.108.x, which is consistent with the parallel releases above:
    • PR #51044 restores the per-user spend breakdown on the aggregated usage route, with an oauthlib 4.0.0→4.0.1 lock bump for a CVE.
    • PR #51362 backports gemini/gemini-decision-1 on /v1/decisions and /v1/systemone.
    • PR #50401 backports Bedrock Converse s3:// media sources.
  • Breaking change (open PR): PR #48846 sends images to Perplexity and OpenRouter decision models. Callers that use drop_params will see changed behavior, since images are no longer dropped or rejected with a 400.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

All of these are open PRs and not yet released:

  • Replicate: PR #51360 adds video generation, image generation and text-to-speech through the predictions API. Until now, replicate/... models only worked for chat.
  • Bedrock: PR #50577 sends s3:// image, document and video URLs to Converse as S3 sources. Today the gateway returns a 500. Non-admin keys are limited to buckets the admin allowlists.
  • Gemini / Perplexity / OpenRouter decision models: see #51362 and #48846.
  • Custom providers: PR #51083 lets custom_provider_map providers serve the native Gemini generateContent route.
  • Provider request: Issue #40112 asks for the IONOS AI Model Hub.
  • Agent clients: PR #51402 adds a Cursor CLI subscription passthrough.
  • Workflows: PR #50384 adds LiteFlow gateway definitions, execution and traces, called as model="workflow/<name>".

4. Performance & Optimization

There are no benchmark numbers in today's data. Resource-efficiency work:

  • PR #51342: fixes Redis connections leaked by each sync run_async_function call. Connections piled up until the client cache evicted them, because per-loop Redis clients were closed after their loop.
  • Issue #50065: since v1.108.0, MCP tools/list blocks for 18–50 s on a legacy subscription listener. This affects clients that send notifications/initialized with a pre-2026 protocol version, such as the Python mcp SDK used by Open WebUI. No fix PR is visible.

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. Budget bypass and leaks
    • #34238: end-user budget can be bypassed through stale per-pod fallback spend after a Redis counter miss.
    • #50534: a streaming client disconnect leaks the Redis budget reservation and causes false 429s. The PR is open.
  2. Cost overbilling
    • #48398: provider-reported usage.cost is trusted as USD without validation, giving up to 1,000,000× overbilling (1.106.3).
    • #39618: cost_per_token crashes on None or string token counts.
  3. Rate limiting
    • #49675: the v3 limiter's TPM counter outlives its window after upstream 429s, so keys are rejected below tpm_limit.
    • PR #51367 holds fallbacks, nested calls, WebSocket turns and oversized prompts to a borrowing team's share. It follows up on six review findings left open after #51328 merged.
  4. Translation correctness
    • #32357: /v1/messages streams thinking_delta inside a text block, plus a duplicate message_start, for reasoning backends. The result is empty content in the Anthropic SDK and Claude Code.
    • #36768: a response.failed event becomes HTTP 200 with an empty finish_reason=stop, so fallbacks never run.
    • #46542: a stream that ends with no finish reason still reports stop.
    • #48145: JSON-defined openai-like providers drop tools when the model is not in the catalog.
    • #42104: mid-conversation system messages break Gemini/Vertex prompt caching (cache_read_input_tokens: 0 on every turn).
    • #47723: Anthropic count_tokens fallback rejects tool_addition and tool_removal blocks.
  5. Config and misc
    • #36095: os.environ/ substitution in numeric params such as weight, rpm or tpm yields a string, so every request to the group returns a 500.
    • #36765: OpenAPI→MCP generation drops request body schemas that use $ref.
    • #33194: non-admins can't assign a budget to personal keys.
    • #36746: OpenTelemetry writes to ended parent spans.
  6. Security hardening: PR #48968 masks token-shaped secrets in spend logs. It is on by default and can be turned off with general_settings.redact_tokens_in_spend_logs: false.

Closed today, mostly through stale cleanup: #12970 (inflated streaming prompt_tokens), #43946 (streamed usage.cost omitted when 0), #31439, #36085.

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Don't rely on gateway budgets alone. Multi-pod Redis deployments have known gaps in end-user budgets (#34238), TPM accounting (#49675) and reservation cleanup on stream disconnects (#50534). Add provider-side caps.
  • Check cost data when you use OpenAI-compatible providers. Provider-reported usage.cost isn't validated (#48398), so cross-check spend against billing.
  • Claude Code and Anthropic SDK clients with reasoning backends (GLM, DeepSeek-R1 via vLLM or SGLang) may get empty content through /v1/messages until #32357 is fixed.
  • MCP users on 1.108.x or later should test tools/list latency (#50065) before upgrading.
  • Resolve numeric config values before startup. Don't use os.environ/ for weight, rpm or tpm (#36095).
  • Bedrock users: s3:// media support is coming, but keep an allowlist of buckets for non-admin keys (#50577).
  • LTS users (1.108.x): you're getting backports (#50401, #51362), and 1.108.6 is out today.

This digest is auto-generated by agents-radar.

item.content:encoded:
AI Open Source Trends 2026-11-12

Sources: GitHub Trending + GitHub Search API | Generated: 2026-11-12 15:44 UTC

AI Open Source Trends Report — 2026-11-12

1. Finds

  • redhat-et/ripwire — A zero-dependency C++23 CLI plus MCP server that gives coding agents compact code signatures (claimed 74.7% fewer bytes than full bodies). It also reports blast radius and tests-to-run after a change. It suits anyone burning context tokens on large repos. Backed by Red Hat's emerging-technologies group, so it is less likely to be an empty shell.
  • ashhart/TensorFold — An LLM inference engine written in Zig, with Metal, CUDA and Vulkan backends. It is worth a look for engineers who want a small, cross-vendor alternative to llama.cpp. It is early and the data gives no benchmarks, so treat it as experimental.
  • drumih/turbo-fieldfare — Runs Gemma 4 26B-A4B in about 2 GB of RAM on M-series MacBooks. Anyone running local MoE models on constrained Macs should try it. The memory claim is striking and should be verified.
  • microsoft/TokenEconomizer — Experience-driven, black-box cost control for coding agents. Teams with large agent bills would want it. It comes from a credible source, but the approach needs testing on your own workloads.
  • openai/codex-security — OpenAI's CLI and TypeScript SDK for finding, validating and fixing security vulnerabilities (+663 today). It is useful for AppSec and CI integration. It is a first-party release, so it is more substantive than most.
  • tigerless-labs/agent-memory — A long-term memory runtime that uses plain Markdown as the source of truth, with local ranked retrieval. Claude Code and Codex can share one store, and it needs no API key. It is for people who want portable agent memory that they can diff and version.

Caution: Several star counts in the topic search are implausibly high for repos this new or niche (for example Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model at 71,127 and cleanyourtv at 56,850). I suspect star inflation, so I did not feature those. Treat any "free unlimited frontier model" plugin with suspicion.

2. Top Projects by Category

🔧 AI Infrastructure

Project Lang Stars (total / today) Summary
redhat-et/ripwire C++ 2,541 A C++23 CLI and MCP server that gives agents compact code signatures, blast-radius analysis and tests-to-run. It targets the context-cost problem of agents reading whole repos.
ashhart/TensorFold Zig 0 (+58) An LLM inference engine for Metal, CUDA and Vulkan, written in Zig. It is a niche alternative to llama.cpp, and it is early.
ggml-org/llama.cpp C++ 0 (+287) The established C/C++ LLM inference library. It is included as a baseline that new engines such as TensorFold are compared against.
drumih/turbo-fieldfare Swift 7,341 Runs Gemma 4 26B-A4B in about 2 GB of RAM on M-series Macs. It is an interesting example of memory-efficient MoE inference.
microsoft/TokenEconomizer Python 5,875 Black-box cost control for coding agents, driven by past experience. It addresses agent token spend directly.
yetone/magpie Go 35,340 A menu-bar tool that routes agent harnesses to other models, such as Codex on DeepSeek or Claude Code on Kimi. It is part of the model-swapping trend.
openai/codex-security TypeScript 0 (+663) OpenAI's security CLI and SDK for finding, validating and fixing vulnerabilities. It is a first-party entry in the security-agent space.

🤖 AI Agents / Workflows

Project Lang Stars (total / today) Summary
addyosmani/agent-skills JavaScript 0 (+812) Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents. It had strong momentum today and comes from a well-known author.
QwenLM/qwen-code TypeScript 0 (+151) An open-source terminal coding agent. It is an established project that is still trending.
CopilotKit/OpenBot TypeScript 11,341 (+291) AI coworkers that each get their own computer, with every action approved beforehand and logged afterward. It works with any AG-UI agent.
Alishahryar1/free-claude-code Python 0 (+461) Claims free tokens across many coding harnesses. It is a proxy-style project, so check the terms of service and sustainability before relying on it.
reason-machines/reason-network Rust 1,733 Lets a team's coding agents communicate with each other. It is a multi-agent coordination layer.
KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop TypeScript 4,694 Lets CLI agents pick up and follow through on tasks in the background. It only asks a human when a decision is uncertain.
tigerless-labs/agent-memory Python 4,315 A Markdown-based long-term memory store with local retrieval, shared between Claude Code and Codex. It needs no API key.
miuuyy/codex-chatgpt-web TypeScript 15,690 Uses ChatGPT Web as a native model inside Codex. It is clever, but it likely depends on terms-of-service gray areas.

📦 AI Applications

Project Lang Stars (total / today) Summary
genspark-ai/genoffice TypeScript 12,233 A free AI office suite for docs, sheets and slides. A CLI and skill let agents edit real .docx, .xlsx and .pptx files locally.
wangzan101/Mika Kotlin 8,365 An on-device Android agent that operates apps and the web. It is a notable mobile agent project.
onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent Swift 4,879 Lets a vision model drive a real iPhone using a $7 ESP32 for AirPlay input and USB HID output. It needs no Mac and no jailbreak.
tangency-labs/solidcraft Rust 15,935 A parametric 3D CAD application in pure Rust, with MCP automation. It is a good example of CAD becoming agent-drivable.
Vincentwei1021/video-shotcraft TypeScript 18,940 A Remotion-based video skill with 124 shot recipes and CapCut export. It is part of the wave of video skills for coding agents.
JuneYaooo/rea-video Python 7,368 Breaks a video down shot by shot into an open VIDEO.md format. It identifies whether each shot was filmed, AI-generated or coded.

🧠 LLMs / Training

Project Lang Stars (total / today) Summary
SoMarkAI/OXR Python 3,796 An open document-parsing model that claims state-of-the-art accuracy and speed. It was post-trained with an RSI loop.
Human-Agent-Society/reef Python 7,804 Infrastructure for agents that continually improve themselves. It sits in the self-improvement research space.
deeplethe/utopia Rust 8,706 Describes itself as an enterprise world model, "world's first" and open source. The claim is bold and needs scrutiny.

🔍 RAG / Knowledge

Project Lang Stars (total / today) Summary
YOLOW92/pagesift Rust 266 A single Rust binary that turns URLs, OCR'd PDFs and Office files into clean Markdown or JSON. It has a Firecrawl/Jina-compatible API and an MCP server.
Zleap-AI/SAG-Wiki Rust 1,105 A lightweight knowledge base for both people and agents, with fast indexing.
sahenjp/RustXNG Rust 959 A self-hosted metasearch and grounding engine for agents, based on SearXNG. It has a JSON API.
Dongbumlee/ontosmith Python 275 Builds governed knowledge graphs from documents. Every fact is traceable to its evidence.
FengZhenfei/carrel Python 805 Ontology-augmented generation for agents. It is a small project in the GraphRAG-adjacent space.

3. Trend Signal Analysis

The strongest attention is on the layer around coding agents, not on new models. That layer includes skills, memory, context compression, cost control, orchestration and model routing. Today's trending list shows it. addyosmani/agent-skills gained +812 stars. Topic results are dominated by SKILL.md-style packages for video, design, charts and geolocation. These target Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI at once, so the SKILL.md format is becoming a de facto cross-harness standard.

Three directions look newer. First, context efficiency: ripwire's signature-based code maps, TokenEconomizer and agent-memory all try to spend fewer tokens per task. Second, MCP is spreading beyond developer tooling into CAD (SolidCraft), office files (genoffice) and web discovery (awesome-webmcp-sites). Third, model-routing shims such as magpie and codex-chatgpt-web decouple the harness from the model vendor.

Industry connections: OpenAI's codex-security shows vendors moving into agentic security. Many repos reference Gemma 4, DeepSeek V4.x and Kimi K3, and local MoE inference is a growing theme (turbo-fieldfare, TensorFold).

A caution on data quality. Many topic-search repos have implausibly high star counts and share branding such as "dsh" and "Jev". That pattern suggests coordinated promotion or star manipulation, and the numbers should not be read as organic momentum.

4. Community Hot Spots

  • Context-budget tooling for agents (ripwire, TokenEconomizer). Token cost is now a daily pain point, so these tools have a direct payoff.
  • Portable agent memory and skills (agent-memory, agent-skills). Plain-file formats that work across harnesses reduce vendor lock-in.
  • Local inference on constrained hardware (turbo-fieldfare, TensorFold). Cross-backend engines and small-RAM MoE are worth benchmarking.
  • Agent security and governance (codex-security, OpenBot). Approve-before-act and audit-after-act designs fit enterprise adoption.
  • Agent-friendly document ingestion (pagesift, OXR). Better parsing improves every RAG pipeline.
